name: Rum
kurzbeschreibung: Largest municipality in the Innsbruck-Land district, featuring the famous Rumer Badlsee and direct access to Innsbruck.
text:
Überblick

Rum is situated in the Innsbruck-Land district directly on the eastern periphery of Tyrol's capital Innsbruck at an altitude of 621 metres, home to around 9,380 residents. The market town extends across the sun-drenched southern slopes of the Nordkette range within the Karwendel Nature Park, reaching from the Inn riverbanks up to the craggy summit of the Rumer Spitze at 2,454 metres. Rum features a dynamic blend of urban convenience and alpine nature. It comprises the historic village centre of Rum-Dorf, the bustling commercial district of Neu-Rum on the valley floor, and Hochrum on the hillside. As one of the traditional MARTHA villages, Rum cherishes living carnival heritage such as the famous Mullerlaufen pageant.

Geschichte

Terraced slopes reveal early settlement traces dating back to antiquity and Roman transport routes along the Inn Valley. The community was first documented between 1152 and 1159 as Rumne in records of the Bavarian Polling Monastery. The name originates from an ancient root meaning fracture or steep break, directly denoting the forces of the Rumer Mure debris torrent. For centuries, recurring mudslides threatened the village until modern torrent and avalanche barriers permanently secured the area. The Late Gothic parish church of Saint George was erected in the 15th century and renovated in Late Baroque style around 1765. In 1987, Rum was formally elevated to the status of market town.

Anreise

Rum enjoys superb transport connectivity. Motorists reach the town via the Inntalautobahn A12, taking exit Hall in Tirol West or Innsbruck-Ost, followed by the B171 or L8 state road within a few minutes. Rum railway station serves as a key junction on the S-Bahn Tirol network (lines S4 and S5), with trains reaching Innsbruck main station in merely four minutes. Additionally, Innsbruck tram lines 2 and 5 alongside several city bus routes provide regular, direct public transit into downtown Innsbruck.

Tipps

A favourite destination for mountain enthusiasts is the year-round Rumer Alm alpine hut (1,243 m), featuring a panoramic sun terrace overlooking the Inn Valley, with a popular toboggan run during winter. Families enjoy the forest playground and nature discovery trail above Hochrum as well as the modern pump track at the riverside sports park. On warm summer days, nearby Lake Roßau on the valley floor offers sunbathing lawns, swimming, and beach volleyball. Experienced mountaineers can tackle the demanding scramble to the peak of the Rumer Spitze (2,454 m) in the Karwendel range.
